title: The Cost Of Protection
gist: Gavekal reports an October 9 understanding in which China accepts a four-year cap on hybrid car exports to the EU, starting at 350,000 vehicles in December 2026 and rising 6% a year, in exchange for the EU toning down its confrontational trade rhetoric (paywalled preview only).

insights.claim: Under the October 9 understanding, Beijing accepted a four-year cap on hybrid exports to the EU starting in December 2026 at 350,000 vehicles, rising 6% annually, which is less than half the European Commission's estimate of 800,000 for 2026.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Limits Chinese hybrid volumes in Europe, a relief for European automakers such as Volkswagen and Stellantis.

insights.claim: China appears to have accepted export restraints in exchange for the EU dialing down confrontational trade rhetoric, giving EU leaders room to ease tensions at the European Council summit on October 15-16.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Watch the summit's tone on China trade; a de-escalation reduces near-term tariff risk.

insights.claim: Chinese brands' share of the European hybrid market jumped from 2% in 2024 to 16% in the first half of 2026, making import restrictions a key EU demand.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Illustrates how fast Chinese share gains can occur and why Europe is pushing back.
